accepted.s: Which one of the following is the fastest form of data transmission and generally provides the highest bandwidth?
accepted.x: Optical fibre transmits data as light pulses and offers the highest speed and bandwidth among the listed media.
accepted.tq: Use the direct comparison and identify the medium with the highest capacity.
accepted.sec: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding optical fibre:
1. It transmits information through light pulses by total internal reflection.
2. It has low signal loss.
3. It is immune to electromagnetic interference.
4. It is the backbone of internet and data connectivity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Optical fibre uses total internal reflection, has low loss, resists electromagnetic interference and forms the backbone of modern internet and data connectivity.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements describe the same transmission medium before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes copper-based transmission media such as twisted pair and coaxial cable?
o: They provide mobility with capacity limited only by satellite position.
They use microwave transmission through geostationary satellites.
They carry electrical signals and are prone to loss and interference over distance.
They carry light pulses and are immune to electromagnetic interference.
accepted.x: Copper media carry electrical signals, have lower bandwidth than optical fibre, suffer loss over distance and are comparatively interference-prone.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the signal type and limitations of copper and optical fibre.
accepted.sec: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

accepted.s: With reference to communication media, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Radio waves — wireless transmission through terrestrial towers
Satellite — negligible latency because of short transmission distance
Optical fibre — mobility with spectrum-limited capacity
Copper cable — transmission by total internal reflection
accepted.x: Radio waves provide wireless terrestrial communication through towers and support mobility, although their capacity is limited by available spectrum. Satellite communication has high latency, while optical fibre uses total internal reflection.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure signal-medium pair and eliminate reversed characteristics.
accepted.sec: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

accepted.s: The high latency associated with geostationary satellite communication is primarily related to the satellite’s approximate distance of:
accepted.x: Geostationary satellites orbit at approximately 36,000 km above the Earth, resulting in relatively high communication latency.
accepted.tq: Match the communication limitation with the characteristic numerical distance.
accepted.sec: Transmission media compared - optical fibre, copper, radio, satellite

accepted.s: Which submarine cable connects Chennai with Port Blair and other islands of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
accepted.x: CANI stands for Chennai–Andaman & Nicobar Islands and connects Chennai with Port Blair and other islands.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and associate it with the locations named in the question.
accepted.sec: Submarine cables and cable landing stations

o: KLI — Chennai to Andaman and Nicobar Islands
accepted.x: KLI is the Kochi–Lakshadweep Islands submarine cable, inaugurated in January 2024. CANI connects Chennai with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

accepted.sec: Submarine cables and cable landing stations

accepted.s: Which organisation was the nodal agency for BharatNet and has subsequently been merged with BSNL?
accepted.x: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL) was the nodal agency for BharatNet and was later merged with BSNL.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation by its specific institutional role rather than by its sector alone.
accepted.sec: Digital connectivity - BharatNet, Digital India, NBM, PM-WANI, railway Wi-Fi

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding BharatNet:
1. It was formerly known as the National Optical Fibre Network.
2. It aims to connect all Gram Panchayats.
3. It is funded by the Universal Service Obligation Fund.
4. Its fibre network involves BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. BharatNet was earlier called NOFN, targets Gram Panchayat connectivity, is funded by USOF and uses the fibre infrastructure of BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
accepted.tq: Verify the programme’s former name, objective, funding source and implementation partners together.
accepted.sec: Digital connectivity - BharatNet, Digital India, NBM, PM-WANI, railway Wi-Fi

accepted.s: As reported for January 2025, the progress of BharatNet was approximately:
o: 3,942 Gram Panchayats connected and 9.78 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats connected and 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
6.92 lakh Gram Panchayats connected and 2.18 lakh km of optical fibre cable laid
2.18 crore Gram Panchayats connected and 6.92 lakh km of copper cable laid
accepted.x: The reported progress was 2.18 lakh Gram Panchayats connected through 6.92 lakh km of optical fibre cable.
accepted.tq: Keep the unit attached to each figure and avoid reversing the two progress indicators.
accepted.sec: Digital connectivity - BharatNet, Digital India, NBM, PM-WANI, railway Wi-Fi

accepted.s:
Which of the following features is associated with the Amended BharatNet Programme?
1. Adoption of a public-private partnership model

3. Provision of 100 Mbps per Gram Panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps
4. Approval involving an outlay of ₹1.39 lakh crore

accepted.tq: Treat the programme’s model, State role, technical target and approved outlay as separate checks.

accepted.s: Which satellite is correctly matched with its principal use?
o: GSAT-6 — Large deployable antenna for mobile and strategic communication
GSAT-11 — First operational satellite of the INSAT system
accepted.x: GSAT-6, launched in 2015, has a large deployable antenna and supports mobile and strategic communication. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A serves the Air Force, and INSAT-1B marked operationalisation of INSAT.
accepted.tq: Start with the satellite-use pair and watch for swapped defence roles and chronology.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - INSAT/GSAT, satellite internet

accepted.s:
Arrange the following satellites in chronological order of the years stated for them:
A. GSAT-7
B. GSAT-6
C. GSAT-7A
D. GSAT-11
accepted.x: The sequence is GSAT-7 (2013), GSAT-6 (2015), GSAT-7A (2018) and GSAT-11 (2018).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest satellite first and then distinguish the two 2018 entries by their stated sequence.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - INSAT/GSAT, satellite internet

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about GSAT-11 is correct?
o: It is a dedicated Navy satellite launched in 2013.
It was the first operational satellite of the INSAT system in 1983.
It is a 2015 satellite with a large deployable antenna for mobile communication.
It is India’s heaviest communication satellite, weighing approximately 5.8 tonnes, and supports high-speed rural broadband.
accepted.x: GSAT-11 is India’s heaviest communication satellite at approximately 5.8 tonnes and is associated with high-speed rural broadband.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive weight and broadband function to separate GSAT-11 from the other satellites.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - INSAT/GSAT, satellite internet

accepted.s: The INSAT system became operational with:
accepted.x: The INSAT system became operational with INSAT-1B in 1983.
accepted.tq: Identify the system’s first operational milestone rather than a later GSAT satellite.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - INSAT/GSAT, satellite internet

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding newspaper registration in India:
1. The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the PRB Act, 1867.
2. The system is administered by the Press Registrar General of India.
3. The earlier designation was Registrar of Newspapers for India.
4. The Press Council Act was enacted in 1978.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 law, the Press Registrar General administers registration, the earlier office was RNI, and the Press Council Act dates from 1978.
accepted.tq: Check the replacement law, present authority, former title and related legislation separately.
accepted.sec: Mass media - AIR, Doordarshan, community radio, newspaper registration

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a media unit associated with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting?
accepted.x: PIB, the Central Bureau of Communication and Publications Division are MIB media units. The Universal Service Obligation Fund is a telecom connectivity funding mechanism, not an MIB media unit.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to telecom funding rather than the listed media-unit group.
accepted.sec: Mass media - AIR, Doordarshan, community radio, newspaper registration

accepted.s:
Arrange the following communication developments in chronological order:
A. First telephone exchange at Calcutta
B. Nationwide mobile number portability
C. Launch of 5G in India
D. Launch of Digital India
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Calcutta telephone exchange (1882), Digital India (1 July 2015), nationwide MNP (3 July 2015) and 5G launch (October 2022).
accepted.tq: Fix the nineteenth-century event first and distinguish the two July 2015 developments before placing 5G.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the communication milestones listed below?
o: Nationwide mobile number portability was introduced on 3 July 2015.
The first telephone exchange was established in Calcutta in 1959.
5G was launched in India in October 2015.
Digital India was launched on 3 July 2015.
accepted.x: Nationwide mobile number portability was introduced on 3 July 2015. Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015, 5G was launched in October 2022, and the first telephone exchange dates to 1882.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced July 2015 dates and reject swapped years.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following best reflects the Andhra Pradesh connectivity initiatives mentioned for 2026?
1. A 100-day drive to complete new telecom towers
2. A planned fibre network in Amaravati
3. A proposed undersea internet cable landing station and data centres
